lines.trans: Hey, did open-house viewing hours not end for the day already?
Yes, they ended—nobody else should know the door passcode.
What are you two up to? Here—catch!
Oh gosh, this bug zapper is what I needed most! Even in a big crowd of people, mosquitoes only bite me.
Senior Joon-mo, how did you know the door code? Senior Ye-jin told me I was the only person she shared it with…
Wait—did I already tell it to you?
Why would anyone need to tell me that? Either your birthday or mine—and sure enough it was mine, May twentieth!

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used as digit string (0520!).

examples.text: 그건 뭐 가르쳐줘야 아냐? 네 생일 아니면 내 생일이지. 내 생일이더구먼, 0520!
examples.trans: Why would anyone need to tell me that? Either your birthday or mine—and sure enough it was mine, May twentieth!
Oh… so zero-five-two-zero is Senior Joon-mo's birthday…

괜찮다.gloss: to be fine; to be okay

meanings.en: to be fine; to be okay; to be alright
meanings.note: Used to reassure someone, decline an offer politely, or say something is acceptable.

examples.trans: I'm really fine.
Is it okay if we meet tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used as present adnominal (구경하는).

examples.text: 승찬이 얘 진짜 예술이야! 새로 들어갈 아파트를 구경하는 집으로 어레인지를 한 거야, 그래서 인테리어 싹 했어!
examples.trans: Seung-chan is a total genius! He arranged my new apartment as a model showroom unit, so I renovated the whole interior!

examples.text: 야, 오늘 구경하는 집 그 시간 끝나지 않았어?
examples.trans: Hey, did open-house viewing hours not end for the day already?

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그것

examples.trans: Where did you buy that?
That is a really good idea.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.en: to end, to finish, to be over
meanings.note: Intransitive verb.

examples.trans: The meeting is already over.
What time does class end?

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Standard polite affirmative response; also used to acknowledge that one is listening.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Yes, I understand.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 통계상 시즌 첫 방송은 전 시즌 마지막 방송보다 2 정도 높았더라고요.
examples.trans: Statistically, a season premiere rated about two points higher than the previous finale.
This expression comes from 'was higher, I found'.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Used as passive casual (물려.).

examples.text: 어머 야, 이거 내가 제일 필요한 건데! 사람들이랑 여럿이 있어도 나만 물려.
examples.trans: Oh gosh, this bug zapper is what I needed most! Even in a big crowd of people, mosquitoes only bite me.
Let us do that (get bitten) right away.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

examples.text: 아니 무슨 비밀번호를 이렇게 바꿔 놨냐?
examples.trans: Wait, why did you change the door code like this?
The topic of passcode, door code came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.

meanings.note: Used as noun + exclamatory copula (생일이네!).

examples.trans: Really? Today is your birthday! Happy day you were born!

examples.text: 그걸 내가 알았니? 준모야, 우리 저녁에 신디 생일 파티 해주자!
examples.trans: How was I supposed to know?! Joon-mo, let us throw Cindy a birthday party tonight!

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: Available time or duration.
Used with native Korean numbers to count hours (한 시간 = one hour).

examples.trans: Do you have time?
It takes two hours.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?

meanings.en: to be how, to be in what state
meanings.note: Its adverbial form 어떻게 ('how') is used to ask how something is done or how things turned out.

examples.trans: How do you feel today?
How did the meeting turn out?

meanings.note: Exclamation of surprise or realization.

examples.trans: Oh my, so nice to meet you!
Oh my, I left my phone behind.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Used as noun + subject (여럿이).

examples.text: 어머 야, 이거 내가 제일 필요한 건데! 사람들이랑 여럿이 있어도 나만 물려.
examples.trans: Oh gosh, this bug zapper is what I needed most! Even in a big crowd of people, mosquitoes only bite me.

meanings.note: Used as casual gift interjection (옜다!).

examples.trans: What are you two up to? Here—catch!

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken contraction of 이것.

examples.trans: How much is this?
Please look at this.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

examples.trans: I'm on my way home right now.

meanings.note: Used as noun + -도 (천장도).
